title: Fix Quickshell notification card geometry
description: Correct the native Quickshell notification-card header layout shown in the attached screenshot: in toast mode the close X sits roughly 40 px too far inward and the application-name cell is unnecessarily constrained. The screenshot's green vertical line is the underlying Hyprland active-window border, not notification chrome.
acceptance_criteria: Toast and notification-center cards anchor the close control at consistent inner-right padding; app name and optional timestamp fill only the remaining header width and elide cleanly; summary, body, progress, and action controls keep their alignment; cards render correctly across short, multiline, action, progress, grouped, and critical notifications.
notes: Before evidence: .beads/attachments/dotfiles-331a-notification-card-geometry.png (15,958 bytes, SHA-256 22dcffa50b125e60eeb30621aa1b9bc542aa7c07b1e1229c60f93b02c9f5c6b3). Diagnosis: toast mode subtracted the invisible timestamp width and an extra spacing slot, pulling the X roughly 40 px inward; the green line is Hyprland active_border, not notification chrome. Implementation: replace the header Row/manual width arithmetic with anchored app name, optional timestamp, and a 28 px right-anchored close target; derive text-column width from the actual icon width and row spacing. Live post-fix evidence: .beads/attachments/dotfiles-331a-notification-card-geometry-fixed.png (370x410 PNG, 36,029 bytes, SHA-256 c44ce41003484eddf76b70abe314e4785f26aaf5698928d510c0ce5b8bc6bd19). Verified original Chrome/action, multiline/two-action, and critical/progress toast variants. qmllint passes, live/source hashes match, Quickshell auto-reloaded with Configuration Loaded and no new QML errors.

Added manual refresh and status IPC methods plus an updater EXIT hook so completion, cancellation, and failure paths request a non-fatal refresh. Existing ProcessJob guards remain, and busy-state policy tests cover idle, official-only, AUR-only, and both-running cases with one coalesced pending refresh. Validation: the correct Qt 6 runner at /usr/lib/qt6/bin/qmltestrunner passed 28 Wayland tests; the source and live integration regression passed; Qt 6 qmllint exited 0 with only two pre-existing shell.qml warnings; bash syntax and diff checks passed; Berg reloaded cleanly and is active in session.slice; Chezmoi is converged. title: Add capped zram and protected systemd-oomd policy
description: Increase zram from the current 4 GiB to a reviewed cap near 32 GiB with zstd and priority 100, then add PSI-based systemd-oomd policy only after Berg, rclone, and critical services are outside or protected from the killable application boundary.
acceptance_criteria: Zram size, compression, and priority are verified; protected services are excluded from the killable boundary; a deliberate pressure test confirms victim selection; rollback is documented.
notes: Implementation and live validation completed. Static validation passed: regression test, bash syntax, yamllint, targeted production ansible-lint, playbook syntax, systemd unit verification, rendered zram-generator validation, and diff checks. Chezmoi applied Berg to session.slice and rclone-box to background.slice with ManagedOOMPreference=omit; both services and the Box mount remained healthy. The first privileged memory-tag invocation was a safe no-op because the new Ansible source had not yet been applied live; after exact Chezmoi apply, activation attempt 2 changed seven items and enabled systemd-oomd. A disposable top-level oomd-test.slice used MemoryHigh=32M, MemoryMax=384M, and a 1 percent for 1 second test threshold. A 256M memhog victim was the only candidate; systemd-oomd selected it at 7.70 percent pressure, the service reported Result=oom-kill, and the test was fully reverted with no stray process. Post-reboot validation: zramctl reports a 32 GiB zstd device, swapon reports 34359734272 bytes at priority 100, oomd is enabled and active, app.slice is monitored at 90 percent swap and 60 percent pressure for 30 seconds, protected services and Box recovered, and no system units are failed.

title: Move active streams when switching audio devices
description: Test current HyprPWCenter behavior, then move active sink inputs and source outputs whenever the default output or input changes so playback and calls follow the selected device. Preserve the Jabra preference chain.
acceptance_criteria: Switching to and from Jabra moves active playback and capture streams; DSP, filter-chain, and EasyEffects streams are not rewired; mute and volume state remain correct.
notes: No additional mover is needed. Live WirePlumber policy already has linking.follow-default-target=true and linking.allow-moving-streams=true; upstream WirePlumber documents that default changes move application playback and capture streams while excluding filter nodes. Controlled test: two disposable null endpoints plus silent pacat playback/capture streams started on endpoint A, then both streams followed a default switch to endpoint B (indexes 222952 to 222981) while volume stayed 100%, mute stayed false, and corked stayed false. The original Ryzen sink/source were restored exactly, their mute states remained intact, and all test streams, sources, sinks, and modules were removed. Jabra was disconnected during validation; this policy is target-agnostic and applies to HyprPWCenter default changes without modifying the existing preference chain.
